Teds Woodworking If you have access to a scroll saw, an electric sander, some glue, varnish, and scraps of different types of wood you can create your own attractive Intarsia wood art. Often a local cabinet shop or lumber yard can be an excellent source of the wood you need and intarsia patterns can be found free on the Internet or in books on the subject.

Attractive Intarsia patterns can be as simple as 8-10 pieces of pine, walnut, or oak carefully cut and fitted together into a whimsical teddy bear, a dozen or two pieces fitted and sanded to make a deer or a bird, or as many as a hundred or pieces skillfully fitted to form an intricate rose or vase of flowers and leaves.

Stains can be used to achieve desired colors but are seldom used in true Intarsia wood art. Often a simple clear lacquer or polyurethane finish is all that is needed once the piece is sanded and glued together. http://quantumvisionsystemreview.com/ryan-shed-plans-review/

Intarsia art can be proudly displayed in your home, given as gifts to others, or sold at craft shows and fairs. Some retirees and stay at home Moms make a good part time income from making and selling pieces at weekend events.
